items.quote: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
items.contrast: Claudius Lysias is the sender, while Governor Felix is the recipient.
items.reason: The letter heading places Claudius Lysias before the “To” line and names Governor Felix after it, clearly distinguishing writer from addressee.

items.quote: took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
items.contrast: Making Uzziah king is the purpose of taking him; Amaziah’s death is the surrounding succession circumstance.
items.reason: The sentence directly connects the people’s taking Uzziah with making him king in his father’s place.

items.quote: Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.
items.contrast: The young man has information for the commander; Paul is the person directing that he be taken there.
items.reason: In Paul’s direct statement, “he” refers to “this young man,” not to Paul.

items.quote: When Zebul the governor of the city heard what Gaal son of Ebed said, he was very angry. Under cover he sent messengers to Abimelek
items.contrast: Zebul sends the messengers, whereas Gaal is the person whose actions Zebul reports.
items.reason: Zebul is the subject introduced before the successive actions of becoming angry and sending messengers under cover.

items.quote: left that town in search of some other place to stay.
items.contrast: The Levite leaves to find somewhere else to stay; arriving at Micah’s house is a later event on his journey, not his stated purpose.
items.reason: The phrase “in search of” explicitly states his reason for leaving, while the next sentence only reports where he subsequently arrived.
